issues.description: The problem statement's UML and text specify that Animal has two attributes (name: String and age: int) and declares a constructor Animal(String, int). The provided solution's Animal class only defines a single-parameter constructor Animal(String) and omits the age attribute entirely. This mismatch between the specified constructor/attributes and the solution implementation is structural and will confuse students about the required Animal API and how to implement subclasses or instantiate Animals.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification, template, and solution consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to show only a name attribute and a constructor Animal(String), or (B) update the solution and template to include the age attribute and provide a constructor Animal(String, int) (and corresponding getter/setter). Ensure all references (examples, Main, and subclass constructors) match the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual description define Animal with an 'age' attribute and a constructor Animal(String, int), but both the template (Main.java usage) and the solution implement Animal and all concrete animal constructors with a single String parameter (Animal(String)) and no 'age' field. This mismatch in the Animal constructor signature / attribute (presence of 'age') creates a conceptual mapping problem: students are instructed to implement an Animal(String, int) with an age attribute but the provided starter code and reference solution use a different constructor shape, causing confusion about the required class API and which signature to follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to require Animal(String) and remove the 'age' attribute/Animal(String,int) constructor, or (B) modify the template and solution to include the 'age' attribute and implement Animal(String, int) (and update all concrete animal constructors and Main.java instantiations accordingly). Choose one canonical signature and ensure all files and examples match it.
